recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If CodeableReference ever renders as generic DataType again, investigate the current publisher/UML generation code path rather than changing the already-correct FHIR source definitions or diagram configuration.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction for R5: CodeableReference datatype displayed in UML as "DataType", with MedicinalProductDefinition cited as the related page/artifact.
initial_application: No commit explicitly tagged FHIR-28171 was found. Zulip shows the report was treated as a bug and linked to the Jira. Source history added CodeableReference as an active datatype in d316758128 and, after the Jira/Zulip report, 7fb17c4549 added CodeableReference to the special datatype diagram configuration; older R5 UML Java tooling history also treated CodeableReference as reference-like, but that tooling is no longer in the current core checkout.
additional_context: Current fhir.ini keeps CodeableReference in build scope, maps it to references.html, and marks it normative. source/datatypes/specialtypes.diagram includes CodeableReference as a distinct class, source/references.html owns the CodeableReference section and datatype include, and MedicinalProductDefinition source elements use code="CodeableReference". Current build.fhir.org MedicinalProductDefinition SVG renders impurity as CodeableReference; its remaining DataType label is for an unrelated choice value[x]. Confluence search found no FHIR-28171 references or conflicting WG evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk met the edit threshold because the current authoritative source and current rendered build already convey the corrected UML behavior for the reported case.
